item.subskill: Area of a slanted triangle by enclosing rectangle
item.grade_rationale: Mid tier for grade 6 (6.G.A.1 and 6.G.A.3): no side lies on a grid line, so the student must box the triangle, find three right-triangle legs from coordinates that cross both axes, halve each, and subtract. About half of grade-6 students complete it; the slips are in reading leg lengths across or below the axes.
item.prompt: On a map in the coordinate plane, each unit stands for 1 meter. A flower bed is shaped like a triangle with corners at (-1, -4), (8, -1), and (2, 6). None of its sides runs along a grid line. What is the area of the flower bed, in square meters?
item.explanation: Draw the rectangle around the triangle: x from -1 to 8 (9 units) and y from -4 to 6 (10 units), area 90. Cut off three right triangles: between (-1, -4) and (8, -1), legs 9 and 3, area 13.5; between (8, -1) and (2, 6), legs 6 and 7, area 21; between (2, 6) and (-1, -4), legs 3 and 10, area 15. Area of the flower bed = 90 - 13.5 - 21 - 15 = 40.5 square meters.
mechanism: enclosing rectangle from the extreme coordinates
three right-triangle corners, each half a rectangle
item.quantity_asked: area of the triangular flower bed in square meters

plugback.why: There is no printed area to check against; an option can only be tested by doing the whole decomposition.

30.misconception: measures a leg along the whole side of the rectangle instead of from the triangle's corner
30.why: For the top-right corner triangle the student takes the horizontal leg as the full width 9 (from x = -1) instead of 6 (from x = 2), so that triangle is 31.5, and 90 - 13.5 - 31.5 - 15 = 30.

45.misconception: thinks any triangle is half of the rectangle around it
45.why: The student halves the enclosing rectangle, 90 / 2 = 45, which is true only when two sides of the triangle lie along the rectangle.

31.5.misconception: finds the distance between two negative numbers by adding their sizes
31.5.why: For the corner triangle below (8, -1), the student reads the vertical leg from -4 to -1 as 4 + 1 = 5 instead of 3, so that triangle is 22.5, and 90 - 22.5 - 21 - 15 = 31.5.

item.intermediate_check: 31.5: no, it is the rectangle minus a wrongly sized corner; 40.5 - 31.5 = 9 is not printed. 30: no, 40.5 - 30 = 10.5, not printed. 45: no, 45 is half the rectangle; the key does not follow from it through one printed number (45 - 40.5 = 4.5). The solved values 90, 13.5, 21, 15 and 49.5 are not options.
item.shape_check: The stem hands over: positive area; area of a triangle with whole-number corners is a whole or half number; less than half the enclosing rectangle (45) unless two sides lie on it, which the stem rules out. 30, 31.5 and 40.5 survive all of these together.
item.interior_parity_check: Middle values 31.5 and 40.5: both have one decimal place ending in .5, same form.
item.arith_class_check: Class: whole or half numbers. Every option is one (30 and 45 whole, 31.5 and 40.5 halves), so the key is not alone.

self_audit.note: Key rank 3 (slot 3). Distractors below the key and their real errors: 31.5 (adding the sizes of -4 and -1 for a vertical leg: a same-sign distance read as if it crossed zero) and 30 (a corner leg measured along the full rectangle side instead of from the triangle's corner). Above: 45 (triangle = half its rectangle). Covering the stem: 30, 31.5, 40.5, 45; the second-smallest (31.5) is a distractor; no ratio hub, no midpoint (the key is not (31.5+45)/2 = 38.25 or (30+45)/2 = 37.5); no option is key +/- a printed number. K1: halves/wholes, all options in class. K2: the only cap is 'less than half the rectangle (45)', which strikes 45 only and leaves a 15-point band below. K3: no pi. K4: whole-number coordinates; no rounding. K5: no table. No distractor is a solved intermediate. Mid tier: a three-corner subtraction with negative coordinates. Cheapest bound strikes one distractor (45). The slip on -4 to -1 is applied to one leg only: it is the only leg between two negative numbers in the problem (the other legs cross an axis or join two positive numbers), so a student who adds sizes for same-sign pairs makes it exactly once. (read) DPAIR 40.5 - 31.5 = 9 = 8 + 1: 9 is the rectangle's width (from -1 to 8), the size of the extra strip the slip adds (2 extra units of leg x 9 / 2); a student cannot read 9 off the stem without finding the width, and no option is the key +/- 9 except through that error. (read) FORM: 30 and 45 are whole, 31.5 and 40.5 halves; areas from whole coordinates can be either. (read) closest MAP MMG-G08 (j=0.46) read: a pentagon with one slanted side split into a rectangle and a triangle; this item boxes a triangle with three slanted sides and subtracts three corners, a different chain.
